rationale: A wins because it keeps turning the founder back toward the proof gate instead of letting the angle cosplay as evidence: the line “A quantified detection-latency gap” is exactly the question that will decide whether this survives a reporter’s second email. B has a useful skeptical frame in “Helio raised $7M to ‘detect wildfires within minutes’ — with zero satellites in orbit and no named customer,” but then steps on a rake with “pre-revenue hardware company”; revenue was not disclosed, which is not the same thing.
gaps_in_A: “A State Fire Agency Agreed to Work With a Satellite Company That Has No Satellites” overstates the MOU. An MOU may be a serious operational agreement or a ceremonial napkin; A knows this in the proof section, but the headline gets ahead of the facts.

“The prevailing assumption is that fire and public-safety agencies require demonstrated, operational capability” is plausible, not proven. If that is the contrarian premise, it needs sourcing or a named procurement norm.
“June timing places this at the opening of Northern Hemisphere fire season” imports an outside seasonal peg. Useful, but not in the supplied update; mark it as context to verify, not as a given.
The category angle says “emerging category” and “category shift” while the refused section correctly says one company is not a trend. That tension needs cleaning up.
gaps_in_B: “pre-revenue hardware company” is invented. The update says revenue is not disclosed, not that Helio has no revenue. That is the kind of tiny confident error that gets a founder in trouble.

“A $7M wildfire-satellite round hints at where earth-observation startups are headed next” tries to build a market shift from one company. B admits it needs “other examples,” which means the angle is not ready as stated.

“Two SpaceX and Planet Labs veterans” and “both founders” assume an exact founder count and background split the update does not provide. Say “founders include ex-SpaceX and ex-Planet Labs backgrounds” until names and tenures are confirmed.

“Next step: find-journalists” is premature. The next move is to resolve the agency name, validation status, launch timeline, and founder credentials; otherwise you are just building a media list for a shaky story.
